style: Handmade science-fiction book illustration, expressive charcoal sketch with visible hand-drawn strokes, soft pastel accents, subtle paper grain, imperfect pencil contours, restrained palette of desert ochre, slate blue, charcoal grey and muted amber, atmospheric natural light, tactile and intimate, clearly illustrated rather than photorealistic. Maintain consistent character designs throughout the trilogy: Koda is a young woman scout with dark hair tied back and practical, weathered expedition gear; Bricole is a palm-sized, asymmetrical tracked robot improvised from mismatched salvaged parts, with exposed cables and a cracked optical sensor; ÉCHO is a tall, smooth silver humanoid guardian with amber eyes. Keep the scene faithful to its chapter and show these characters when they are present; after Bricole's sacrifice, represent Bricole only through the small salvaged parts Koda carries, never as a living robot.
